Employment Type: Full-time for the duration of the primary campaign. Role Summary: The Regional Organizing Director is a core member of the campaign’s grassroots operation, responsible for executing day-to-day voter contact and volunteer organizing across New Hampshire’s First Congressional District. This role is designed to build, mobilize, and sustain a statewide field program through phone banks, postcards, canvassing, and county-level coordination. This role requires ability to work evenings and weekends as needed. Key Responsibilities and Deliverables: Recruit, train and manage volunteers in your region to execute a voter persuasion and ID program. Execute weekly phone banks and canvasses. Distribute call lists, scripts, and canvassing materials; ensure volunteers are prepared and supported. Conduct follow-up outreach to deepen volunteer engagement and development. Maintain regular communication with core supporters. Support execution of local organizing plans, events, and outreach efforts. Track volunteer participation, voter contact metrics, and organizing activity. Maintain accurate and up-to-date records in campaign databases. Collaborate with the communications and digital teams to amplify campaign support, events, and organizing efforts. Work closely with political, communications, and digital teams to align organizing efforts. What We Value for This Position: Tireless work ethic and flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed. Willingness to travel extensively throughout New Hampshire. Strong ethical standards, professionalism, and commitment to confidentiality. Excellent time management and ability to work independently and collaboratively. Positive, can-do attitude with a genuine passion for public service and campaign work. Respectful and collegial demeanor. Commitment to Democratic politics, the values, vision, and goals of the campaign. Experience and Skills: **Required:Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, and ability to travel across the state. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain relationships with diverse stakeholders. Strong organizational and research skills with exceptional attention to detail. Proficiency with Google Suite and familiarity with campaign tools (NGP/VAN or similar systems) a plus, not a requirement. Experience in digital organizing and digital content creation is a plus, but not required. Experience in political campaigns, advocacy, or community organizing (internships or campus organizing experience welcome) preferred. Willingness to work long hours. Compensation: Salary: $4,500 per month, commensurate with experience. The campaign offers a monthly healthcare stipend. This is a full-time position for the duration of the campaign. Looking for candidates to start immediately. Interested applicants should send a resume and letter of interest to Political/Organizing Director, Nick Sperduto by April 30: [email protected] Equal Opportunity/Diversity Policy: Maura Sullivan for Congress is committed to an inclusive and equitable environment and diversity among its staff and recognizes that its continued success requires the highest commitment to engaging, retaining, and supporting a diverse staff that provides the best quality services to supporters and constituents. Maura Sullivan for Congress is an equal opportunity employer, and it is our policy to recruit, hire, train, promote and administer any and all personnel actions without regard to sex, race, age, color, creed, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, physical or mental disability, personal appearance, marital status, family responsibilities, genetic information, or any other legally protected basis. Maura Sullivan for Congress will not tolerate any unlawful discrimination and any such conduct is strictly prohibited.
